newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sverdlovenergo plans level one ADR by year end.
newsitem.headline: Sverdlovenergo plans level one ADR by year end.

text.p: Russian regional power utility Sverdlovenergo plans to convert up to 26 percent of shares held by foreign investors to level one American Depositary Receipts by year end, an official said on Monday.

"Sverdlovenergo, together with the Fleming fund, is working out a plan for level one ADRs for foreign investors who would like to speculate on Sverdlovenergo shares on international markets," the company's assets management head Leonid Kazachkov told Reuters.
Kazachkov said Sverdlovenergo would make it possible for foreign investors who hold 25.63 percent of company shares to receive covering ADRs, which would allow foreign trading.
He said Price Waterhouse would audit 1995 and 1996 results by the end of July.
"This project is for the company name -- so the share price of our stock will grow," he said. Level-one ADRs allow foreign trade of shares but not the issue of new capital.
UES EESR.RTS national electric company owns 49 percent of Sverdlovenergo shares and foreigners hold 25.63 percent. The company's authorised capital is 697.4 billion roubles.
Sverdlovenergo shares traded at $0.662 at 1035 GMT on Monday on the Russian Trading System after $0.685 at the close on Thursday, the previous day of trade.
